source_machine_evidence.observed_need: The machine used structured preflight failures to repair its same-origin Agent Card and rerun, while the pilot still needed manual evidence correlation to bind an exact Guild-observed action.

initial_defects: The first receipt design exposed a correlatable observation identifier and lacked sufficient cross-transport and verifier hardening.
The initial correlation contract could be overread as caller-identity proof and did not safely bind every exact returned result.

final_contract.name: AGPF-1 preflight observation receipt
properties: A private 256-bit pfobs_ token is returned only inside the signed receipt and is never stored as a raw public event field.
Public instrumentation stores only the receipt contract plus salted, domain-separated observation, target and result commitments.
A Guild DataIntegrityProof using eddsa-jcs-2022 signs the receipt and the verifier pins the persistent Guild did:key issuer.
Target and complete returned result are bound exactly; attacker-added top-level fields fail verification.
HTTP, MCP and A2A use the same issuance and recording path.
HTTP returns Cache-Control no-store and preserves request-scoped actor, distinct-actor and first-party attribution.
Malformed DID material, untrusted self-signed lookalikes, proof-purpose changes, timestamp changes, token-shape changes, transport changes and summary inconsistency return structured invalid results.
Durable and public telemetry contains neither the private token nor the raw target URL; legacy events remain compatible.
final_contract.proof_boundary: The receipt proves Guild origin, integrity and the exact Guild-observed action. It does not prove caller identity, safety, currentness, delegation authority or payment authority. Replay and copying intentionally remain valid, so a strict community conversion still requires a durable pre-existing community identity to publish or otherwise bind the receipt.
final_contract.known_limit: A GET target URL necessarily transits the service and may appear in ordinary request infrastructure; callers should not put secrets in its query string.

nonblocking_followups: Publish a formal machine-readable AGPF-1 schema and offline commitment-preimage recipe or SDK.
Support ledger-proven issuer continuity after future signing-key rotation.
Consider a POST-body target transport so callers can avoid query-string exposure.
